q: Can my EU subsidiary's Guarantees of Origin cover electricity at our Indian factory?
title: Can EU GOs cover an Indian factory?
short: No. Guarantees of Origin are issued for electricity produced in Europe, and the GHG Protocol requires certificates to come from the same market where the power is used. The Indian grid is not connected to Europe's, so EU GOs cannot lower your Indian factory's market-based Scope 2.

p: Among the Scope 2 Quality Criteria in the GHG Protocol guidance, one decides this case: a certificate must be sourced from the market where the covered electricity is consumed. RE100's technical criteria apply the same idea. India and the EU are separate grids with no physical exchange of power, so a GO cannot describe electricity your factory could have received.

sections.h: What the EU rules say about GOs
p: GOs are issued under Article 19 of the Renewable Energy Directive, Directive (EU) 2018/2001, for renewable power produced in a member state, and the directive lets member states recognise third country GOs only where the EU has an agreement with that country and energy is directly imported or exported. Neither applies to India.

sections.h: What the Indian factory can use instead
ul: India RECs under the CERC REC Regulations, 2022.
A green tariff from your discom, or green open access power.
A captive or group captive renewable plant, or a PPA with the attributes kept with you.
p: Each must be retired or contracted in the name of the Indian entity for the same reporting year.

Report market-based Scope 2 site by site. The EU subsidiary can apply its GOs to its own EU consumption. The Indian factory's uncovered kWh use the CEA grid factor, since India publishes no residual mix. Report location-based figures for every site as well.

example.title: Worked example: a 3,000 MWh Indian factory
lines: GOs for 3,000 MWh bought by the EU subsidiary: not valid for India, so market-based = 3,000,000 x 0.710 = 2,130,000 kg, 2,130 t CO2
I-RECs or India RECs for 3,000 MWh of Indian generation, retired for the same year: market-based 0 t
Location-based in both cases: 2,130 t CO2, reported alongside

senseible: Senseible works out location-based Scope 2 for each site from its electricity bills. Give it the instrument type, quantity and generation period and it adds a market-based figure per site. Buying, retiring and validating certificates stays with you and the registry.
